payout_quote: Owners pay a 11.5% service fee for domestic U.S. transactions or 14.5% service fee for international fees.
steps: Create a free GetMyBoat owner account and list your boat or watercraft (kayaks and small craft accepted from verified businesses only, per 2024 standards) with photos, availability, pricing, and requirements.
Respond to renter inquiries, vet guests, and approve booking requests or send custom quotes.
Complete the rental trip; GetMyBoat holds the payment and transfers it to you only upon successful completion of the trip.
Receive your payout (booking value minus the 11.5% US / 14.5% international service fee) via your chosen payout method; note PayPal may add its own fees.
catches: GetMyBoat takes an 11.5% service fee from owners on US transactions (14.5% international) plus renters pay up to 13% + a flat $20 service fee, which can suppress your effective rate.

Earnings are fully variable: you set the price but income depends on boat type, location, season, and demand; 'average owner earns $25,000 annually' is a marketing claim, not a guarantee - most owners earn far less.
Boats are expensive assets to expose: damage, wear, fuel, maintenance, slip fees, and insurance costs come out of your pocket; always document pre/post-trip condition.

You are responsible for legal compliance: captained charters have Coast Guard licensing rules; bareboat rules apply for self-drive rentals; check state boating laws, registration, and insurance requirements.
New 2024 standards: kayaks, canoes, paddleboards, and jetskis are only accepted from verified and registered businesses - individuals can't list those.
Rental income is taxable; payouts held until trip completion, so cancellations mean no payout per your cancellation policy.
Seasonal and weather-dependent: demand collapses in off-season.
biggest_catch: GetMyBoat keeps 11.5-14.5% of every booking and there is no guaranteed income: earnings are entirely demand-driven, the 'average $25,000/year' owner figure is marketing not typical, and you carry the full cost and risk of operating an expensive boat for strangers.
eligibility: Must own or be authorized to rent the watercraft; comply with federal/state boating laws (USCG captain licensing for captained charters; bareboat rules for self-drive). Since 2024, small craft (kayaks, SUPs, jetskis) only accepted from verified businesses. 170k+ listings in 184 countries per GetMyBoat.
timing: Listing is free and self-serve; payout is released only upon successful completion of the trip. First booking depends on market demand and season and can take weeks or months.
